prompts.text: In an AVL tree, the absolute difference between the heights of a node's left and right subtrees is at most ______.

answers.evidence_quote: |height(v.leftSubtree) - height(v.rightSubtree)| ≤ 1

prompts.hint: It represents a minimal numerical threshold for height imbalance.
prompts.explanation: AVL trees strictly maintain balance by requiring subtrees to differ in height by no more than 1.

prompts.text: The propagation procedure that pushes an inserted element up to restore the heap condition is called ______.

answers.evidence_quote: This propagation is sometimes called heapifyUp

prompts.hint: The path moves upward toward the root of the tree.
prompts.explanation: When a new element is inserted, heapifyUp moves it up until the heap order condition is satisfied.

prompts.text: In a B-tree, when a leaf becomes empty after a deletion, this condition is known as ______.

answers.evidence_quote: This sometimes called “underflow”

prompts.hint: The term for having fewer items than required.
prompts.explanation: Underflow occurs when a leaf loses its contents below the allowed capacity during deletion.

prompts.text: A binary search tree where the height difference between the left and right subtrees of every vertex is at most 1.

answers.evidence_quote: AVL tree is a Binary Search Tree, with the following property: For vertex v of the tree |height(v.leftSubtree) - height(v.rightSubtree)| ≤ 1

prompts.hint: Named after creators Adelson-Velsky and Landis.
prompts.explanation: An AVL tree is a self-balancing binary search tree defined by its height-balance invariant.
